title: HDF System
description: Describes a system's authorization boundary, components, and interconnections. Maps to OSCAL SSP system-characteristics and FedRAMP system inventory.

systemId.description: Stable UUID (RFC 4122) for this system. Enables cross-document correlation independent of file location. Optional in casual use, expected in production documents.

owner.description: Team or individual responsible for this system's authorization and compliance. Maps to OSCAL responsible-party with role 'system-owner'.

name.description: Human-readable system name. Example: 'Enterprise Portal Production'.

identifier.description: System identifier from an authoritative source. Example: eMASS system ID, FedRAMP package ID.

identifierScheme.description: URI identifying the scheme of the system identifier. Example: 'https://emass.mil', 'https://fedramp.gov'.

description.description: Description of the system's purpose and mission.

authorizationDate.description: Date the current authorization status was granted. ISO 8601 format.

boundaryDescription.description: Description of the system's authorization boundary. Example: network CIDR blocks, cloud VPC IDs, physical locations.

components.description: System components within the authorization boundary. Uses the full polymorphic Component type with stable identity (componentId), external references, and SBOM support.

controlDesignations.description: Declares which controls are common, hybrid, or system-specific, and which component provides them. Maps to NIST SP 800-53 control designations and OSCAL leveraged-authorizations.

dataFlows.description: Inter-component data flows describing how components communicate. Supports local, cross-system, and external flows. Replaces the interconnections[] field.

labels.description: Optional key-value labels for grouping and querying systems.

integrity.description: Cryptographic integrity information for verifying this system document has not been tampered with.

generator.description: Information about the tool that generated this system document.

components.name: WebTier
components.description: RHEL 9 web servers running the portal

https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.title: HDF Common Primitives
https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.description: Shared building blocks used by hdf-results and hdf-baseline schemas.

Hash_Algorithm.description: Supported cryptographic hash algorithms for checksums and integrity verification.
Hash_Algorithm.title: Hash Algorithm

id.description: The unique identifier for the group. Example: the relative path to the file specifying the requirements.

title.description: The title of the group - should be human readable.

requirements.description: The set of requirements as specified by their ids in this group. Example: 'SV-238196'.

Requirement_Group.description: Describes a group of requirements, such as those defined in a single file.
Requirement_Group.title: Requirement Group

branch.description: The branch name for a git repo.

path.description: The relative path if the dependency is locally available.

statusMessage.description: The reason for the status if it is 'failed' or 'skipped'.

git.description: The location of the git repo. Example: 'https://github.com/my-org/ubuntu-22.04-stig-baseline.git'.

supermarket.description: The 'user/profilename' attribute for a Supermarket server.

compliance.description: The 'user/profilename' attribute for an Automate server.

examples.statusMessage: Unable to clone repository: authentication failed

Dependency.description: A dependency for a baseline. Can include relative paths or URLs for where to find the dependency.
Dependency.title: Dependency

anyOf.description: A human readable/meaningful reference. Example: a book title.
A URL pointing at the reference.
A URI pointing at the reference.

Reference.description: A reference to an external document.
Reference.title: Reference

ref.description: Path to the file that this requirement originates from.

line.description: The line on which this requirement is located.

Source_Location.description: The explicit location of a requirement within source code.
Source_Location.title: Source Location

platformName.description: The platform name - can include wildcards. Example: 'debian'.

platform.description: The location of the platform. Can be: 'os', 'aws', 'azure', or 'gcp'.

release.description: The release of the platform. Example: '20.04' for 'ubuntu'.

Supported_Platform.description: A supported platform target. Example: the platform name being 'ubuntu'.
Supported_Platform.title: Supported Platform

algorithm.description: The hash algorithm used for the checksum.

Checksum.description: Cryptographic checksum for baseline integrity verification.
Checksum.title: Checksum

type.description: The type of identifier. Use 'email' for email addresses, 'username' for user accounts, 'system' for automated systems, 'simple' for basic string identifiers without additional classification, or 'other' for custom identity systems.

description.description: Optional description of the identity or identity system, particularly useful when type is 'other'.

Identity.description: Represents an identity that performed an action, such as capturing evidence or applying an override.
Identity.title: Identity

type.description: The type of evidence being provided.

data.description: The evidence content. For screenshots/files: base64-encoded data or URL. For code/logs: the raw text. For URLs: the URL string.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this evidence shows.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the evidence. Example: 'image/png', 'text/plain', 'application/json'.

encoding.description: Encoding used for the data. Example: 'base64', 'utf-8'.

size.description: Size of the evidence data in bytes.

capturedAt.description: Timestamp when this evidence was captured. ISO 8601 format.

capturedBy.description: Identity of who or what captured this evidence.

examples.description: Link to security ticket documenting remediation work

Evidence.description: Supporting evidence for a finding or override, such as screenshots, code samples, log excerpts, or URLs.
Evidence.title: Evidence

uri.description: URI pointing to automated remediation resources (Ansible playbooks, Terraform scripts, etc.). Examples: GitHub repository, DISA STIG Supplemental Automation Content, vendor-provided scripts.

checksum.description: Optional cryptographic checksum for verifying the integrity of remediation resources fetched from the URI. Recommended for security when referencing external automation scripts.

Remediation.description: Reference to automated remediation resources for implementing security controls. Points to external automation content like Ansible playbooks, Terraform scripts, or vendor-provided remediation tools.
Remediation.title: Remediation

type.description: The type of verification method. Example: 'JsonWebKey2020', 'RsaVerificationKey2018', 'Ed25519VerificationKey2020'.

controller.description: The entity that controls this verification method. Can be a DID, URI, or other identifier.

publicKeyJwk.description: Public key in JSON Web Key format.

publicKeyPem.description: Public key in PEM format. Example: '-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----...-----END PUBLIC KEY-----'.

publicKeyBase58.description: Public key in Base58 format, commonly used with Ed25519 keys.

Verification_Method.description: Verification method containing the public key needed to verify a digital signature. Supports multiple key formats including JWK (for RSA, EC), PEM, and Base58.
Verification_Method.title: Verification Method

description.description: Description of this milestone or task.

completedBy.description: Identity of who completed this milestone.

Milestone.description: A milestone or task within a POA&M remediation plan.
Milestone.title: Milestone

created.description: When the signature was created. ISO 8601 format.

creator.description: The identity that created this signature.

signatureValue.description: The base64-encoded or base58-encoded signature value.

proofPurpose.description: The purpose of this signature. Example: 'attestation', 'authentication', 'assertionMethod'.

verificationMethod.description: The verification method containing the public key for signature verification.

nonce.description: Random value to prevent replay attacks.

challenge.description: Challenge value from the verifier, used in challenge-response authentication.

domain.description: Domain restriction for the signature, prevents cross-domain replay attacks.

creator.description: Hardware security module (HSM) for automated attestations

Signature.description: A digital signature following W3C Data Integrity Proofs pattern. Supports hardware security tokens (PKCS#11/PKCS#12), Yubikeys, GPG keys, passkeys, and other cryptographic signing methods via JWK, PEM, or Base58 key formats.
Signature.title: Signature

title.description: The title - should be human readable.

copyrightEmail.description: The email address or other contact information of the copyright holder(s).

summary.description: The summary. Example: the Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) header.

supports.description: The set of supported platform targets.

labels.description: Optional key-value labels for flexible grouping. Well-known keys: system, component, environment, region, team. Values must be strings.

Baseline_Metadata.description: Shared metadata fields for baselines. Used in both standalone baseline documents and evaluated baseline results.
Baseline_Metadata.title: Baseline Metadata

label.description: Description category. The 'default' label is required for the primary description. Common labels: 'default', 'check', 'fix', 'rationale'. Tools may use custom labels.

descriptions.description: Array of labeled descriptions. At least one description with label 'default' must be present. Convention: place default description first. Common labels: 'default', 'check', 'fix', 'rationale'.

refs.description: The set of references to external documents.

tags.description: A set of tags - usually metadata like CCI, STIG ID, severity.

code.description: The raw source code of the requirement. Set to null for manual-only requirements or requirements not yet implemented. Note that if this is an overlay, it does not include the underlying source code.

sourceLocation.description: The explicit location of the requirement within the source code.

Requirement_Core.description: Core requirement fields shared between baseline requirements and evaluated requirements. Contains the fundamental requirement definition without assessment results.
Requirement_Core.title: Requirement Core

Severity.description: Severity rating for a requirement. Typically derived from the numeric impact score.
Severity.title: Severity

https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.title: HDF System Primitives
https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.description: Types for describing system architecture, authorization boundaries, and components.

Authorization_Status.description: Authorization to Operate (ATO) status for the system.
Authorization_Status.title: Authorization Status

baselineRef.description: Name of the baseline this override applies to. If omitted, applies to all baselines that define this input.

inputName.description: Name of the input being overridden. Must match an Input.name in the referenced baseline.

value.description: The overridden value. Should match the type of the original input.

justification.description: Rationale for why this override is needed.

approvedBy.description: Identity of the person or system that approved this override.

Input_Override.description: An override of a baseline input value for a specific component. Enables system-specific tailoring of baseline parameters.
Input_Override.title: Input Override

Target_Selector.description: A label selector that matches targets by label key-value pairs. All specified labels must match (AND logic). Example: { "labels.component": "WebTier" } matches targets with labels.component = "WebTier".
Target_Selector.title: Target Selector

controlId.description: The control identifier (e.g., 'SC-7', 'AC-2 (1)'). Must match a NIST tag in a baseline requirement's tags.

designation.description: NIST SP 800-53 control designation. 'common': fully provided by another component or system. 'system-specific': implemented by the inheriting component(s) only. 'hybrid': shared responsibility between provider and inheritor.

providedBy.description: componentId of a local component that provides this control. Omit when the provider is an external system.

systemRef.description: Reference to another hdf-system document whose component provides this control. Use when the provider is in a different system. Omit when the provider is local.

inheritedBy.description: componentIds that inherit this control. If omitted, all components in the system inherit it.

description.description: Justification for this designation — who provides the control, why it's inherited, and any relevant authorization references.

examples.description: User identification and authentication provided by Keycloak SSO via SAML 2.0.
Physical access authorizations provided by AWS GovCloud per FedRAMP High authorization.

Control_Designation.description: Declares a control's designation within a system — whether it is common (provided by another component or system), system-specific (implemented locally), or hybrid (shared responsibility). Maps to NIST SP 800-53 Appendix C control designations and OSCAL SSP by-component provided/inherited semantics.
Control_Designation.title: Control Designation

https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.title: HDF Component Primitives
https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.description: First-class system component with identity, polymorphic type, SBOM embedding, and system-binding properties. Components are the successor to Targets, adding stable identity (componentId), external system cross-references, and software inventory.

type.description: Component type discriminator. Same values as Target types.

componentId.description: Stable UUID (RFC 4122) for this component. Required in hdf-system documents, optional in hdf-results. Enables cross-document correlation, diffing, and data flow references.

description.description: Description of this component's role or purpose.

owner.description: Team or individual responsible for this component. Enables per-component ownership when different teams manage different parts of a system.

externalIds.description: Map of external identifier scheme to value. Well-known schemes: aws (instance ID), azure (resource ID), cmdb (asset ID), emass (system ID), cve (CVE ID). Custom schemes are allowed.

labels.description: Optional key-value labels for flexible grouping. Well-known keys: system, component, environment, region, team. Values must be strings.

sbom.description: Embedded CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM document representing this component's software inventory. The sbomFormat field determines which format constraints apply.
sbom.$comment: Validated conditionally: CycloneDX requires bomFormat='CycloneDX' + specVersion; SPDX requires spdxVersion + SPDXID. Full SBOM schema validation is a tool-level concern.

sbomRef.description: URI reference to an external CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM document for this component. May be a relative path, absolute URI, or fragment identifier.

sbomFormat.description: Format of the SBOM (embedded or referenced). Required when sbom or sbomRef is present.

baselineRefs.description: Names of baselines that apply to this component.

inputOverrides.description: System-specific overrides for baseline input values.

targetSelector.description: Label selector to match targets belonging to this component during migration. Targets with matching labels are automatically included.

bomFormat.description: Must be 'CycloneDX' for CycloneDX SBOM documents.

Base_Component.description: Base properties shared by all component types. Extends the Target concept with stable identity, external references, and SBOM embedding.
Base_Component.title: Base Component

Component.description: A system component. Uses discriminated union pattern with 'type' field as discriminator. Superset of Target with identity, external IDs, and SBOM support.
Component.title: Component

macAddress.description: MAC address in colon-separated hexadecimal format.

Host_Component.description: A physical or virtual server, workstation, or network device.
Host_Component.title: Host Component

image.description: Image the container was started from.

namespace.description: Namespace within the cluster, if applicable.

Container_Platform_Component.description: A container orchestration platform (Kubernetes, OpenShift, ECS, etc.).
Container_Platform_Component.title: Container Platform Component

Cloud_Account_Component.description: A cloud provider account (AWS account, Azure subscription, GCP project).
Cloud_Account_Component.title: Cloud Account Component

region.description: Cloud region where the resource resides.

Cloud_Resource_Component.description: A specific cloud resource (EC2 instance, S3 bucket, Azure VM, etc.).
Cloud_Resource_Component.title: Cloud Resource Component

Application_Component.description: A running application or API (for DAST tools).
Application_Component.title: Application Component

Artifact_Component.description: A software artifact or dependency (for SCA tools).
Artifact_Component.title: Artifact Component

Network_Component.description: A network segment or network device.
Network_Component.title: Network Component

https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.title: HDF Data Flow Primitives
https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.description: Types for describing data flows between components within a system and across system boundaries. Data flows model network connections, API calls, database queries, and other inter-component communication.

systemRef.description: URI reference to the hdf-system document containing the target component. May be a relative path, absolute URI, or fragment identifier.

componentId.description: UUID of the component in the referenced system.

Cross_System_Reference.description: Reference to a component in a different system document, enabling cross-boundary data flow modeling.
Cross_System_Reference.title: Cross-System Reference

external.description: Must be true. Discriminator indicating this endpoint is outside all modeled systems.

description.description: Human-readable description of the external endpoint. Example: 'Third-party payment gateway (Stripe API)'.

External_Endpoint.description: An endpoint outside all modeled systems (e.g., a third-party API, public internet, or partner system not represented in HDF).
External_Endpoint.title: External Endpoint

Data_Flow_Endpoint.description: A data flow endpoint: either a local component (UUID), a component in another system (cross-system reference), or an external endpoint outside all modeled systems.
Data_Flow_Endpoint.title: Data Flow Endpoint

oneOf.description: UUID of a component in the current system.

from.description: UUID of the local component that is one end of this data flow. Always references a component in the current system document.

to.description: The other end of this data flow. Can be a local component (UUID), a cross-system component reference, or an external endpoint.

direction.description: Data flow direction. 'unidirectional' means data flows from→to only. 'bidirectional' means data flows in both directions (e.g., request/response).

description.description: Human-readable description of this data flow's purpose and the data exchanged.

authentication.description: Authentication mechanism used for this connection. Examples: 'mTLS', 'OAuth2', 'API key', 'SAML', 'Kerberos'.

examples.description: REST API calls from WebTier to API Gateway
Database queries from API Gateway to PostgreSQL
SAML authentication requests to central auth system

Data_Flow.description: A data flow between two endpoints. The 'from' endpoint is always a local component; the 'to' endpoint can be local, cross-system, or external. Use 'direction' to indicate whether data flows one-way or both ways.
Data_Flow.title: Data Flow

https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.title: HDF Extension Primitives
https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.description: Extension types for waivers, attestations, generators, and integrity.

type.description: The type of status override applied to this requirement.

status.description: The new status this override sets for the requirement. This intentionally changes the compliance status.

reason.description: Explanation for why this status override was applied.

appliedBy.description: Identity of who applied this status override. For simple cases, use type 'simple' with just an identifier.

appliedAt.description: Timestamp when this status override was applied. ISO 8601 format.

expiresAt.description: Timestamp when this status override expires and must be reviewed/renewed. REQUIRED - no permanent status overrides allowed. ISO 8601 format.

signature.description: Optional digital signature for enhanced trust and non-repudiation. Supports hardware security tokens (PKCS#11/PKCS#12), Yubikeys, GPG keys, passkeys, and other signing methods.

evidence.description: Supporting evidence for this status override, such as screenshots demonstrating manual verification for attestations.

previousChecksum.description: SHA-256 checksum of the previous amendment in chronological order. Creates a tamper-evident chain of amendments (similar to blockchain). Null for the first amendment on a requirement.

examples.reason: This control does not apply to containerized environments as the application runs in ephemeral containers without persistent storage
Manual verification completed: Reviewed firewall rules and confirmed all required ports are properly restricted per security policy

Status_Override.description: An intentional change to a requirement's compliance status (waiver or attestation). Status overrides change the effectiveStatus of the requirement. All status overrides must have an expiration date to enforce periodic review.
Status_Override.title: Status Override

type.description: The type of POA&M. 'remediation' fixes root cause. 'mitigation' reduces risk via compensating controls. 'riskAcceptance' documents decision to accept risk.

explanation.description: Detailed explanation of the plan, including what actions will be taken.

appliedBy.description: Identity of who created this POA&M. For simple cases, use type 'simple' with just an identifier.

appliedAt.description: Timestamp when this POA&M was created. ISO 8601 format.

expiresAt.description: Optional expiration date for this POA&M requiring review/renewal. ISO 8601 format.

milestones.description: Optional array of milestones tracking progress toward completion.

signature.description: Optional digital signature for enhanced trust and non-repudiation.

evidence.description: Supporting evidence for this POA&M, such as documentation of compensating controls or mitigation implementation.

previousChecksum.description: SHA-256 checksum of the previous amendment in chronological order. Creates a tamper-evident chain of amendments (similar to blockchain). Null for the first amendment on a requirement.

examples.explanation: Upgrade OpenSSL to version 3.0.x to address CVE-2024-XXXXX vulnerability. Root cause: outdated dependency version in base image.

milestones.description: Update base Docker image to use OpenSSL 3.0.x
Verify vulnerability no longer present via security scan

examples.explanation: Implement network segmentation as compensating control while awaiting vendor patch for database vulnerability. Traffic to vulnerable database server is restricted to internal management VLAN only.

appliedBy.description: Automated POA&M creation from vulnerability scan

milestones.description: Configure firewall rules to restrict database access to management VLAN
Monitor for vendor security patch release

POAM.description: Plan of Action and Milestones for tracking remediation, mitigation, or risk acceptance. POAMs do NOT change the effectiveStatus - the requirement remains in its current state while the POA&M tracks remediation efforts.
POAM.title: POAM

name.description: The name of the software that produced this HDF file. Example: 'gosec-to-hdf'.

version.description: The version of the tool. Example: '5.22.3'.

Generator.description: Information about the tool that generated this HDF file.
Generator.title: Generator

name.description: The name of the security tool that produced the data. Examples: 'gosec', 'Semgrep', 'OpenSCAP', 'AWS Config', 'Nessus'. Omit if the tool cannot be identified.

version.description: Version of the source tool, if available in the tool's output. Example: '5.22.3'.

format.description: The file format, if it is a recognized named format shared by multiple tools. Examples: 'SARIF', 'XCCDF'. Omit for tool-specific formats where the tool name already implies the format (Nessus XML, gosec JSON).

Tool.description: The security tool that produced the assessment data represented in this HDF file. Aligns with SARIF, OSCAL, and CycloneDX terminology.
Tool.title: Tool

algorithm.description: The hash algorithm used for the checksum.

signedBy.description: Identifier of who signed this file.

Integrity.description: Cryptographic integrity information for verifying the HDF file has not been tampered with. If algorithm is provided, checksum must also be provided, and vice versa.
Integrity.title: Integrity

https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.title: HDF Amendment Primitives
https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.description: Types for waivers, attestations, exceptions, and POA&Ms that modify requirement compliance status.

Override_Type.description: The type of amendment. 'waiver': risk accepted (AO). 'attestation': manually verified (assessor). 'exception': not applicable (system owner + AO). 'poam': remediation tracked (no status change). 'inherited': control provided by another component or system (overrides to notApplicable/passed).
Override_Type.title: Override Type

requirementId.description: The ID of the requirement being amended. Must match a requirement ID in the referenced baseline.

baselineRef.description: Name of the baseline containing the requirement. Required when the system has multiple baselines with potentially overlapping requirement IDs.

status.description: The new status this amendment sets. For POA&Ms, this is the current status (POA&Ms track work, they don't change status).

appliedBy.description: Identity of who applied this amendment.

appliedAt.description: When this amendment was applied. ISO 8601 format.

expiresAt.description: When this amendment expires and must be reviewed. No permanent amendments. ISO 8601 format.

previousChecksum.description: Checksum of the prior amendment in the chain. Creates a tamper-evident linked list. Null for the first amendment.

milestones.description: Remediation milestones (primarily for POA&M type amendments).

inheritedFrom.description: componentId of the local component that provides this control. Set when the provider is in the same system. Omit for external or cross-system providers; the reason field explains the source. Primarily used with type 'inherited'.

componentRef.description: componentId of the component this amendment is scoped to. When set, the amendment only applies to the specified component. When omitted, the amendment applies system-wide.

examples.reason: Compensating control: session timeout set to 15 min

evidence.description: ISSM approval with compensating control documentation

examples.reason: Patch requires vendor release, expected Q2 2026
IA-2 is a common control provided by Keycloak SSO. This application has no local authentication mechanism.

Standalone_Override.description: A standalone amendment that modifies a requirement's compliance status. Extends the inline Status_Override concept with requirementId and baselineRef for use outside of results documents.
Standalone_Override.title: Standalone Override

https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.title: HDF Result Primitives
https://mitre.github.io/hdf-libs/schemas.description: Types for representing assessment results and statuses.

Result_Status.description: The status of an individual test result. 'notApplicable' indicates the requirement does not apply to the target. 'notReviewed' indicates the requirement was not assessed (e.g., requires manual verification).
Result_Status.title: Result Status

status.description: The status of this test within the requirement. Example: 'failed'.

codeDesc.description: A description of this test. Example: 'limits.conf * is expected to include ["hard", "maxlogins", "10"]'.

runTime.description: The execution time in seconds for the test.

startTime.description: The time at which the test started.

resource.description: The resource used in the test. Example: 'file', 'command', 'service'.

resourceId.description: The unique identifier of the resource. Example: '/etc/passwd'.

message.description: An explanation of the test result. Typically provided for failed tests, errors, or to explain why a test was not applicable or not reviewed.

exception.description: The type of exception if an exception was thrown.

backtrace.description: The stacktrace/backtrace of the exception if one occurred.

Requirement_Result.description: A test within a requirement and its results and findings such as how long it took to run.
Requirement_Result.title: Requirement Result

Requirement_Description.description: A labeled description for a requirement, such as fix text or check instructions.
Requirement_Description.title: Requirement Description
